profiles.bio: Home cook passionate about traditional Malay cuisine. Nasi Lemak is my love language.
Weekend warrior in the kitchen. Roti canai and teh tarik keep me going every morning.
Culinary school grad sharing Malaysian recipes with a modern twist. Sambal is my superpower.
Hawker stall kid turned home chef. Char kway teow and mee goreng are in my DNA.
Baker by hobby, kuih enthusiast by heart. Anything pandan-flavoured makes me happy.
Laksa lover and spice addict. Always hunting for the best bowl in KL.
Wok enthusiast. High heat, smoky flavour — that's the secret to everything.
Tom Yam fanatic and self-taught cook. Making Thai-Malay fusion happen one bowl at a time.
Rempah is my therapy. Grinding spice pastes the old-fashioned way, no shortcuts.
Nyonya Peranakan food is my heritage. Cooking grandma's recipes so they're never forgotten.

recipes.title: Nasi Lemak
recipes.description: The quintessential Malaysian breakfast dish featuring fragrant rice cooked in coconut milk and pandan leaves. Served with sambal, crispy anchovies, roasted peanuts, cucumber slices, and a hard-boiled egg. Every Malaysian has a favourite version.
steps: Wash rice and soak for 30 minutes, then drain.
Cook rice with coconut milk, pandan leaves, and salt in a rice cooker or pot until fluffy.
Blend dried chillies, shallots, and belacan into a smooth paste for the sambal.
Fry the sambal paste in oil until fragrant, then add tamarind water, sugar, and salt. Simmer until thick.
Deep-fry the dried anchovies until crispy and golden.
Dry-fry or bake peanuts until crunchy.
Hard-boil the eggs and slice the cucumber.
Serve rice with sambal, anchovies, peanuts, cucumber, and egg.

recipes.title: Beef Rendang
recipes.description: A rich and tender dry curry originating from the Minangkabau people of West Sumatra, deeply beloved across Malaysia. Beef is slow-cooked in an aromatic coconut milk and spice paste until the liquid evaporates and the meat is caramelised. Best enjoyed with ketupat or nasi impit.
steps: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, turmeric, and dried chillies into a fine rempah paste.
Heat oil in a wok and fry the paste with lemongrass until fragrant and the oil separates.
Add beef pieces and stir to coat in the paste.
Pour in coconut milk and bring to a boil, then reduce to a low simmer.
Add kaffir lime leaves and tamarind water. Season with salt and sugar.
Simmer uncovered for 2–3 hours, stirring occasionally, until liquid is almost gone.
Add toasted coconut (kerisik) and continue cooking until meat is dark and dry.
Serve with steamed rice or ketupat.

recipes.title: Curry Laksa
recipes.description: A hearty and spicy coconut curry noodle soup that is a staple of Malaysian hawker culture. The rich, fragrant broth is made from a blended spice paste and finished with coconut milk. Topped with tofu puffs, prawns, bean sprouts, and a dollop of sambal.
steps: Soak dried shrimp and blend with shallots, lemongrass, dried chillies, and turmeric into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil until aromatic and oil rises to the surface.
Add coconut milk and water, then bring to a gentle boil.
Add tofu puffs, fish balls, and prawns. Simmer until cooked.
Season with salt and sugar to taste.
Cook vermicelli separately and divide into serving bowls.
Ladle hot broth and toppings over the noodles.
Garnish with bean sprouts, fried shallots, and sambal on the side.

recipes.title: Char Kway Teow
recipes.description: A beloved Malaysian street food of flat rice noodles stir-fried over very high heat in a screaming-hot wok. The signature wok hei (breath of the wok) smokiness makes this dish unforgettable. Made with eggs, prawns, bean sprouts, and chives in a savoury soy-based sauce.
steps: Heat wok over maximum heat until smoking. Add oil.
Fry garlic until golden, then add chilli paste.
Add prawns and toss until they start to turn pink.
Add flat rice noodles and quickly toss in the wok.
Add dark soy sauce and light soy sauce. Toss to coat evenly.
Push noodles to the side, crack eggs into the wok and scramble briefly.
Add bean sprouts and chives, toss everything together for 30 seconds.
Serve immediately while still hot and smoky.

recipes.title: Mee Goreng Mamak
recipes.description: A popular Indian-Muslim fried noodle dish found at mamak stalls all across Malaysia, open late into the night. Yellow egg noodles are stir-fried in a rich tomato-based sauce with tofu, egg, and boiled potatoes. The tangy, slightly sweet sauce is the heart of this dish.
steps: Boil potatoes until soft, then cut into small cubes.
Deep-fry tofu until golden, then slice.
Heat oil in wok and fry shallots and garlic until fragrant.
Add tomato sauce, chilli sauce, and soy sauce. Stir to combine.
Add noodles and toss vigorously to coat in the sauce.
Push noodles aside, fry egg and scramble into noodles.
Add bean sprouts, potatoes, and tofu. Toss for 1 minute.
Serve with lime wedges and sliced green chilli.

recipes.title: Roti Canai
recipes.description: A flaky, layered flatbread brought to Malaysia by South Indian immigrants and now a breakfast institution. The dough is stretched and folded repeatedly to create hundreds of flaky layers, then cooked on a flat griddle with ghee. Best dipped into dhal or chicken curry.
steps: Mix flour, salt, condensed milk, egg, and water into a soft dough. Knead for 10 minutes.
Divide dough into balls, coat with ghee, and rest for at least 4 hours.
Stretch each dough ball on an oiled surface until paper-thin.
Fold the stretched dough into a square parcel.
Cook on a greased flat griddle over medium heat until golden and crispy on both sides.
Fluff the roti by clapping between both hands to separate the layers.
Prepare dhal by simmering lentils with onion, cumin, and curry powder.
Serve roti warm with dhal and curry on the side.

recipes.title: Chicken Satay
recipes.description: Skewered and grilled chicken marinated in a fragrant blend of spices, served with a rich peanut dipping sauce, ketupat, and cucumber. Satay is a quintessential Malaysian party food and street snack. The key is a good marinade and charcoal grilling.
steps: Blend lemongrass, shallots, and spices into a marinade paste.
Marinate chicken pieces in the paste with sugar and salt for at least 2 hours.
Thread marinated chicken onto bamboo skewers.
Grill over charcoal or a hot grill pan, basting with oil.
Turn skewers every 2 minutes until charred and cooked through.
For peanut sauce, blend peanuts, dried chillies, shallots, and tamarind. Fry the paste, add coconut milk, and simmer until thick.
Serve satay with peanut sauce, ketupat rice cakes, and cucumber slices.

recipes.title: Tom Yam Soup
recipes.description: A fiery and sour Thai-influenced soup that has been fully adopted into Malaysian hawker culture. Loaded with prawns, mushrooms, and fish, this soup is intensely aromatic from lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and galangal. A squeeze of fresh lime at the end brightens every flavour.
steps: Bring water or stock to a boil in a pot.
Add bruised lemongrass, galangal slices, and kaffir lime leaves.
Add chilli and tomato quarters. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add prawns, mushrooms, and fish balls.
Season with fish sauce, sugar, and lime juice.
Taste and adjust balance of sour, spicy, and salty.
Serve hot, garnished with fresh coriander.

recipes.title: Nasi Goreng
recipes.description: The definitive Malaysian fried rice, best made with day-old rice so each grain separates perfectly in the wok. Dark soy sauce gives it a rich, caramelised colour while chilli paste adds heat. Often topped with a fried egg, fried anchovies, and sliced cucumber.
steps: Heat oil in wok until very hot. Fry garlic and shallots until golden.
Add chilli paste and stir-fry for 30 seconds.
Add cooked rice and toss vigorously, breaking up clumps.
Add dark soy sauce and light soy sauce. Toss until evenly coloured.
Push rice aside, fry an egg to your liking.
Mix egg through the rice and add spring onions.
Fry anchovies separately in oil until crispy.
Serve rice topped with fried egg, crispy anchovies, and cucumber slices.

recipes.title: Curry Mee
recipes.description: A rich, golden noodle soup with a curry-coconut broth that is deeply warming and complex. Popular across Klang Valley and Penang, each region has its own variation. This version features a bold rempah base, thick coconut milk broth, and toppings of pork-free alternatives like tofu and prawns.
steps: Blend shallots, lemongrass, dried chillies, turmeric, and curry powder into a smooth paste.
Fry paste in oil until fragrant and oil separates.
Add water and bring to a boil. Simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in coconut milk and reduce to a gentle simmer. Do not boil vigorously.
Add prawns, tofu puffs, and cook until done.
Season with salt and sugar.
Cook noodles separately and divide into bowls.
Ladle broth and toppings over noodles. Garnish with bean sprouts and mint.

recipes.title: Asam Pedas
recipes.description: A tangy and spicy fish stew that is a beloved Malay home-cooking staple, especially in Johor and Melaka. The sourness from tamarind and the heat from dried chillies create a perfectly balanced broth. Best eaten with plain white rice to absorb all the gorgeous sauce.
steps: Blend shallots, dried chillies, belacan, galangal, and turmeric into a paste.
Fry the paste in oil with lemongrass until fragrant.
Add tamarind water and bring to a boil.
Add fish, tomato, and okra. Simmer gently so fish doesn't break up.
Season with sugar and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes until fish is cooked and broth is flavourful.
Serve hot over steamed white rice.

recipes.title: Bubur Ayam
recipes.description: A comforting Malaysian-style chicken congee made by slow-cooking rice until it breaks down into a silky, thick porridge. Topped with shredded poached chicken, crispy shallots, fresh ginger, and soy sauce. Perfect for rainy days or when you need something gentle and nourishing.
steps: Simmer chicken in water with ginger and garlic until cooked. Remove and shred.
Use the chicken broth and add rice. Simmer on low heat, stirring occasionally.
Cook for 45–60 minutes until rice breaks down into porridge consistency.
Season porridge with salt and white pepper.
Fry sliced shallots in oil until golden and crispy. Set aside.
Serve congee topped with shredded chicken, crispy shallots, spring onion, and a drizzle of soy sauce and sesame oil.

recipes.title: Cendol
recipes.description: A beloved Malaysian iced dessert consisting of green rice flour jelly noodles, red beans, coconut milk, and palm sugar syrup poured over shaved ice. The combination of sweet gula melaka, creamy coconut milk, and cold ice is absolutely addictive on a hot day.
steps: Extract pandan juice by blending pandan leaves with water and straining.
Mix rice flour and tapioca flour with pandan juice. Cook over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Press hot mixture through a cendol mould into iced water to form green jelly strands.
Simmer gula melaka with water until a thick syrup forms. Cool.
Warm coconut milk with a pinch of salt. Cool.
Fill bowls with shaved ice, add cendol jelly strands and red beans.
Drizzle coconut milk and gula melaka syrup generously over the top.

recipes.title: Apam Balik
recipes.description: A crispy Malaysian pancake turnover filled with creamy sweet corn, crushed roasted peanuts, and butter. Known as a popular street snack sold from roadside stalls and pasar malam night markets. The edges are crispy while the centre remains soft and fragrant.
steps: Mix flour, sugar, baking powder, eggs, coconut milk, and a pinch of salt into a smooth batter.
Rest batter for 15 minutes.
Heat a round non-stick pan over medium-low heat and lightly grease.
Pour a ladleful of batter and swirl to coat the pan evenly.
Cover and cook until bubbles form and surface is set.
Spread butter, crushed peanuts, and sweet corn over one half.
Fold pancake in half to enclose filling.
Remove and slice. Serve warm.

recipes.title: Kuih Lapis
recipes.description: A beautiful steamed layered kuih made from rice flour, tapioca flour, coconut milk, and sugar, usually in alternating red and white layers. Each thin layer is steamed individually before the next is added, requiring patience but producing a stunning result. A classic at every Malaysian celebration.
steps: Mix rice flour, tapioca flour, sugar, coconut milk, pandan water, and salt into a smooth batter.
Divide batter in half. Colour one half red with food colouring.
Grease a square steaming tray and preheat over steamer.
Pour first layer (white) thinly and steam for 4–5 minutes until set.
Pour second layer (red) and steam again for 4–5 minutes.
Repeat alternating layers until all batter is used.
Steam final layer for 10 minutes to ensure it is fully set.
Cool completely before cutting into portions with a wet knife.

recipes.title: Sambal Nasi Lemak Fusion Bento
recipes.description: A modern bento-style take on Nasi Lemak that replaces the traditional banana leaf presentation with a meal-prep-friendly bento box. Comes with sambal-marinated grilled chicken instead of the usual fried chicken, plus all the classic sides. Great for office lunches with a twist.
steps: Cook coconut milk rice with pandan leaves and salt.
Blend sambal base from dried chillies, shallots, belacan, and tamarind.
Marinate chicken thighs in half the sambal paste overnight.
Cook remaining sambal paste in a pan, add tamarind water and sugar to make sambal.
Grill marinated chicken until charred and cooked through.
Fry anchovies until crispy; dry-roast peanuts until fragrant.
Assemble bento: rice moulded with a cup, sliced chicken, sambal, anchovies, peanuts, and cucumber.
Seal bento box and refrigerate if packing for later.

recipes.title: Smoky Char Kway Teow with Lap Cheong
recipes.description: A halal-friendly variation of classic Char Kway Teow that replaces traditional pork sausage with beef lap cheong for a smoky-sweet hit. Cooked over maximum heat to achieve proper wok hei, this version stays true to the original's DNA while being accessible to all Malaysians.
steps: Slice beef lap cheong diagonally and set aside.
Heat wok until visibly smoking. Add oil.
Fry garlic until fragrant, add chilli paste.
Add lap cheong and sear until edges caramelise.
Add prawns and toss until pink.
Add flat rice noodles, dark soy sauce, and light soy sauce. Toss aggressively.
Push noodles aside, add egg and scramble into the noodles.
Add bean sprouts and chives, toss for 30 seconds. Serve immediately.

recipes.title: Rendang Ayam Putih
recipes.description: A lighter, white-style rendang made with chicken instead of beef, forgoing dried chillies for a pale, fragrant version using only fresh aromatics and coconut milk. Less fiery than traditional rendang but no less complex. Pairs beautifully with saffron or turmeric rice.
steps: Blend shallots, garlic, ginger, galangal, candlenut, and white pepper into a pale rempah.
Fry rempah with lemongrass in oil until fragrant and cooked through.
Add chicken pieces and coat well in the paste.
Pour in coconut milk and add kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer uncovered over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally.
When liquid reduces by half, add toasted coconut (kerisik).
Continue simmering until sauce is thick and clings to the chicken.
Season to taste and serve with warm rice.

recipes.title: Pandan Coconut Cendol Pudding
recipes.description: A creative no-churn dessert that reimagines traditional cendol as a sliceable coconut pandan pudding, perfect for serving at gatherings. Layers of pandan jelly and coconut milk jelly are stacked and chilled to create a stunning cross-section. Drizzled with gula melaka syrup to serve.
steps: Extract fresh pandan juice by blending pandan leaves with water and straining.
Mix first jelly layer: pandan juice, agar agar powder, sugar, and a pinch of salt. Heat until dissolved.
Pour thin pandan layer into a greased rectangular tray. Cool until just set.
Mix second layer: coconut milk, agar agar powder, sugar, and salt. Heat gently.
Pour coconut milk layer over the set pandan layer.
Repeat alternating layers until all mixture is used.
Refrigerate until fully set, at least 4 hours.
Slice and serve drizzled with warm gula melaka syrup.

recipes.title: Tom Yam Butter Prawns
recipes.description: A bold fusion of classic Malaysian butter prawns and Thai tom yam flavours, creating a dish that is creamy, spicy, sour, and utterly addictive. The butter sauce is infused with lemongrass, kaffir lime leaves, and chilli. Serve with crusty bread or plain rice to mop up the sauce.
steps: Clean and devein prawns, leaving shells on for flavour.
Bruise lemongrass and galangal. Roughly chop chilli and kaffir lime leaves.
Melt butter in a wide pan over medium heat.
Fry garlic, lemongrass, galangal, curry leaves, and chilli until fragrant.
Add prawns and toss to coat in the butter aromatics.
Add fish sauce, lime juice, and a pinch of sugar. Toss for 2 minutes.
Continue cooking until butter sauce turns golden and coats the prawns.
Serve immediately with crusty bread or steamed rice.

posts.caption: Tried something new this week — Nasi Lemak bento boxes for meal prep! Grilled chicken instead of fried, and honestly? Zero regrets 😍 Swipe to see the inside of the box #nasilemak #mealprep #recilink
Aishah's Nasi Lemak bento recipe is a game changer!! Made this for my office lunch today, everyone was jelak in the best way 🙏 Full recipe on Recilink!
Finally cracked the halal Char Kway Teow code 🔥 Beef lap cheong is the move, trust me. Wok hei was absolutely on point tonight #charkwayteow #halal #woklife
Weekend cooking session with the family 🥢 Made Hafiz's halal CKT recipe and the kids approved!! The lap cheong gives it such a nice smoky sweetness 😋
Rendang Ayam Putih — my grandmother's recipe, finally documented on Recilink! The colour is so different from normal rendang but the aroma is incredible 🌿 No chilli, just pure rempah goodness
Made this Cendol Pandan Pudding for my sister's kenduri and everyone kept asking for the recipe! It's on Recilink now 💚 so pretty when you slice it #pandan #cendol #kuih
Honestly didn't expect this pandan pudding to be so easy to make. Nurul's recipe is foolproof! Already made it twice this week 😂 #recilink #pandanlover
Tom Yam Butter Prawns is the recipe nobody asked for but everyone needed 🦐🧈🌶️ The butter sauce with lemongrass hits DIFFERENT. Get the recipe on my Recilink! #fusion #prawns #tomyam

comments.content: Tried this for my family's breakfast, semua orang suka! Sambal dia memang sedap gila 😭
The sambal recipe is spot on! I added a bit more belacan and it was perfect.
Rendang took 3 hours but worth every second. Mine came out SO dark and caramelised 🙌
Pro tip: double the kerisik. You won't regret it. Rendang level up!
Laksa broth was incredible! I added extra tofu puffs because why not lah 😂
First time making laksa from scratch and it tasted exactly like my favourite hawker stall. Terharu betul!
Wok heat is everything for this dish. Finally got proper wok hei at home after the 4th attempt!
Made this for dinner, husband said it's better than the mamak version. High praise!
Day-old rice makes such a huge difference, don't skip that step! Sedapnya 😋
Cendol turned out so good! The gula melaka syrup is the star of the show honestly.
Love this bento idea! Made it for my kids' school lunch and they loved it. Creative gila!
The grilled chicken version is actually healthier AND tastier. Dah jadi my weekly meal prep now!
Beef lap cheong is genius!! Never thought of using it for CKT. Wok hei was on fire 🔥
This white rendang is so underrated! My mak used to make something similar. Thank you for sharing this recipe 🥺
The colour is so beautiful and the fragrance from the lemongrass and kaffir lime is heavenly. A keeper!
Made this for raya open house and it was gone in 10 minutes. Everyone kept asking for the recipe!
The layering technique is therapeutic lah! Took time but the end result is cantik gila. 10/10 would make again.
Tom Yam butter prawns is the most Malaysian-Thai fusion I've ever tasted and I'm obsessed 🦐🔥
Cooked this last weekend, the butter sauce is ridiculous good! Served with baguette and chef's kiss.
Asam Pedas Johor style is my comfort food! This recipe is very close to my auntie's version. Terima kasih!
